## Findings
- claim-1: Schur functions are homogeneous by partition weight; \(\Lambda/I_{r,n-r}\) inherits this grading, with multiplication truncated to partitions in \((n-r)^r\). [doi:10.1112/jlms.12832, lines 263-269]
- claim-2: \(\omega(s_\lambda)=s_{\lambda'}\) is a ring involution, hence preserves Littlewood–Richardson multiplication under conjugation. [doi:10.1112/jlms.12832, lines 481-485]
- claim-3: For the non-self-conjugate pair \[ [222,4^5]\subset\Lambda/I_{5,4},\qquad [33,5^4]\subset\Lambda/I_{4,5}, \] complete \(A_+J\)-relation matrices and quotient Smith data in weights \(6,\ldots,20\) agree: free ranks are \[ (1,1,2,1,1,0,\ldots,0), \] in weights \(6,\ldots,20\), and all torsion-factor lists are empty. [artifact 5b6e59b74af1b386568e8d3014cdef276ec80f89225cf5ba2367c73fa3b0a993]
- claim-4: Conditional on accepted quotient conjugation and ideal correspondence, partition conjugation induces an integral graded isomorphism \[ J_v/A_+J_v\;\cong\;J_{v^\vee}/A^\vee_+J_{v^\vee}, \] preserving degreewise integral torsion subgroups and free ranks.
## Strategy
Let \(q=n-r\), \(A=\Lambda/I_{r,q}\), \(A^\vee=\Lambda/I_{q,r}\), and interpret the right-hand \(A_+\) as \(A^\vee_+\). Conditional on accepted quotient conjugation and ideal correspondence,  
\[
\Omega(\bar s_\lambda)=\bar s_{\lambda'}
\]
is an integral graded ring isomorphism \(A\cong A^\vee\) with
\[
\Omega(J_v)=J_{v^\vee},\qquad \Omega(A_+)=A^\vee_+.
\]
Thus, degreewise,
\[
\Omega\bigl((A_+J_v)_d\bigr)
=\Omega\!\left(\sum_{e>0}A_eJ_{v,d-e}\right)
=\sum_{e>0}A^\vee_eJ_{v^\vee,d-e}
=(A^\vee_+J_{v^\vee})_d.
\]
Hence \(\Omega\) descends to integral graded isomorphisms
\[
(J_v/A_+J_v)_d\cong
(J_{v^\vee}/A^\vee_+J_{v^\vee})_d
\]
for every partition-weight degree \(d\). Therefore their torsion subgroups, invariant factors, and free \(\mathbb Z\)-ranks agree. The \(a=0\) singleton-family boundary is included in the accepted ideal-correspondence premise.
